result:
I've written and run the A15 Reporting acceptance suites. Four tests fail on purpose because they expose three product defects; everything else passes, including all the existing QA suites. This was an authoring task, not a gate review, so I give no verdict. Changes are uncommitted on `dg5/qa-c` at HEAD `bb0601f6` (unchanged from the start), and took about 42 minutes (21:15:50 to 21:57:58 UTC).

**What I wrote**
- **Support module** (`tests/qa/support/a15.ts`): exports a report through the real API, delivers the job to the real worker export runner, downloads the file and reads it back with the package's own readers.
- **Four integration suites** (`tests/qa/integration/a15-*.test.ts`):
  - all 12 report definitions × every format each one offers × English and Arabic (64 files);
  - the filtered RAID register and the gate pack slides, plus formula-injection checks;
  - the synthetic demo transformation (International Roaming);
  - issued snapshots, executive and meeting packs, the meeting presentation and the meeting cut-off draft agenda.
- **One e2e spec** (`e2e/a15-reporting.spec.ts`), run in chromium-en and chromium-ar.

**Checks, with real exit codes**

| Check | Exit | Result |
|---|---|---|
| DG4 historical validator, start and end | 0 / 0 | PASS both times |
| Full `tests/qa` integration run | 1 | 206 tests in 19 files: 202 pass, 4 fail (the defects below) |
| e2e spec, en and ar, on the real stack | 0 | 2 passed; axe found 0 serious or critical issues |
| `pnpm lint` | 0 | |
| Repo-wide prettier check from the assignment | 0 | |
| Mutation checks in a disposable copy | — | 6 of 6 made their target tests fail for the expected reason |

`node_modules` is read-only in this sandbox, so plain `vitest run` fails at start-up. Every Vitest run therefore used `--configLoader runner`, which loads the same config without writing to `node_modules`. The handback also lists the earlier failed runs, all caused by my own fixture mistakes, which I fixed.

**Product defects found** (proposed IDs; the orchestrator allocates the real ones)
- **F-DG5-qa-c-2 (High, proposed mandatory violation):** reports and exports generated in a demo database carry no "Illustrative example — synthetic" / "مثال توضيحي — اصطناعي" label, and demo snapshots don't record that they are synthetic. ADR-0050 §2(d) and REQ-PB-089 require both. None of the 54 demo exports has the label; the word "illustrative" appears only inside some English record text.
- **F-DG5-qa-c-1 (Medium):** XLSX and CSV exports omit the B0004 provenance statement; ADR-0046 §2 says every file carries it. PDF, DOCX and PPTX do include it. 14 files are affected.
- **F-DG5-qa-c-3 (Medium):** no product export ever contains a system SUM total formula. No report assembler emits a total, so the "a system SUM total remains a formula" half of REQ-S13-006 can't happen.
- **Low observations:**
  - The Arabic snapshot page's SHA-256 checksum runs past the card edge, and its source-records table shows raw codes (`register`, `raid_entry`).
  - The Arabic gate pack deliberately prints an English catalogue-label column alongside the Arabic one; I treat that as data, not a missing translation.
  - KPI targets print unrounded, as `100.000000`.

**Not covered**
- The REQ-S09-011 "current metrics" are checked only for presence, not compared with the dashboard values.
- The REQ-S13-008 provisional label is proven on the demo benefits-register PDF, not on an executive-pack PDF with a pending benefit.
- The e2e stack runs no worker, so the e2e export stays queued; file contents are proven only through the integration suites.
- Arabic layout is checked by text order and direction markers, not by looking at rendered PDF pages.

Everything is in `docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG5/qa/T-DG5-QA-C-authoring/`; `handback.md` has the requirement-to-test table, the mutation table and the exact request and response for each defect, next to the logs, screenshots and mutation logs.
